decisive_spans.text: a homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left, with adjacent right upper-lobe infiltrates

an 11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura, with a nodular pleural component, mass effect on the right hilum, supra-aortic vessels, and superior vena cava, pneumomediastinum, left pneumothorax, and lytic destruction with cortical fracture of the T1 and T2 vertebrae

response.rationale: The presence of a large mediastinal mass with lytic destruction of vertebrae strongly supports Germ cell tumor. While Thymic carcinoma can cause a mediastinal mass, the specific bone destruction is a key differentiator.
